summary: 40 min / 11 completed experiments, averaging 4 min each. The supplied closeout timing was dominated by Full-Scale Pipeline v3 gate churn: 14 min + 6 min + 5 min for the Exp 1414 repair-executor path, or 25/40 min total. The legacy Exp 1269 arXiv Bundle v10 gate consumed another 10 min. Both RTX 3090s were idle at closeout, with 4 MB allocated and 0% utilization on each GPU, and gpu_monitor.py reported no processes. The next milestone can plausibly run about 55% faster if weak gates, same-verdict reruns, legacy arXiv blocks, and GPU scheduling telemetry are fixed.
timing_data_caveat: The supplied slowest-experiment list names Exp 1414, Exp 1419, and Exp 1269 paths from the .109 repair/arXiv carry-forward chain. This artifact uses that supplied timing as the authoritative .110 operational-retro input, while using exp1425-exp1438 only for .110 roadmap context.

research_milestone_context.context_summary: Milestone .110 reached the research threshold with repair-v2 prototype evidence, DVI v3 deployed, PRM/DPO/latent work advanced, and FR-11 growth plus missing RTL source carried forward. This operational retro focuses on execution efficiency, not research claims.

slowest_experiments.name: Full-Scale Pipeline v3 - Gated on Exp 1414 Repair Executor
slowest_experiments.why_slow: The full-pipeline task was allowed to run after the repair executor was merely deployed. The gate did not require a nonzero accepted-repair count, so expensive validation could proceed even when the repair path had not proven useful.

slowest_experiments.name: arXiv Bundle v10 - Gated on Exp 1269 Critical Fixes
slowest_experiments.why_slow: A legacy publication-path gate remained load-bearing. The conductor spent a runtime slot rediscovering a known blocked or manually-gated arXiv state instead of emitting an activation-time terminal block.

slowest_experiments.name: Full-Scale Pipeline v3 - Gated on Exp 1414 Repair Executor
slowest_experiments.why_slow: This appears to be duplicate same-verdict pipeline churn for the same exp1419 artifact class. After a zero-success/full-pipeline-miss verdict, exact reruns should be suppressed until the repair executor or candidate pool changes.

slowest_experiments.name: Full-Scale Pipeline v3 - Gated on Exp 1414 Repair Executor
slowest_experiments.why_slow: Same failure class as the 6 min duplicate entry: repeated validation on unchanged repair evidence consumed wall time without changing the conclusion.

slowest_experiments.name: Doomed-rerun block: SOTA GGUF Cache + Provenance Preflight - P
slowest_experiments.why_slow: Cache/provenance readiness was checked as a scheduled runtime slot. This should be a sub-second activation preflight that writes explicit missing-model or provenance fields.

questions_answered.which_experiments_took_longest_and_why: Full-Scale Pipeline v3 was the dominant path: 25 minutes across three same-task entries. The root cause was a weak gate predicate that treated repair-executor deployment as enough evidence to run pipeline validation. The second-largest path was the 10 minute Exp 1269 arXiv Bundle v10 legacy gate.
questions_answered.was_gpu_utilization_efficient: No. The supplied and verified gpu_monitor.py snapshots show both RTX 3090s at 4/24576 MB and 0% utilization, with no processes. This indicates idle scheduling capacity, not useful parallel model execution.
questions_answered.were_there_zombie_processes: No material GPU zombies were present. gpu_monitor.py reported an empty process list and no warnings. The 4 MB per-GPU allocation is below the monitor's zombie threshold and is consistent with baseline driver allocation.
questions_answered.could_any_experiments_have_been_parallel: Yes. In the supplied timing, duplicate Full-Scale Pipeline v3 reruns should have been retired rather than parallelized. In the .110 DAG, independent CPU/lightweight work such as test-debt mapping, rejection-ledger analysis, DPO provenance audit, latent-repair analysis, and hardware-source existence checks could overlap with gated repair/pipeline work. Qwen and Gemma repair lanes should run through DualGPURunner when live model inference is actually needed.
questions_answered.was_preflight_test_suite_a_bottleneck: Not in the top-five wall-time data. The only preflight-like item listed was a 2 minute SOTA GGUF cache/provenance block. However, .110 test-debt artifacts still show full-suite/spec-coverage risk, so global preflight should stay focused and cluster-scoped until the suite is green.
questions_answered.were_doc_reconciliation_passes_efficient: Docs were not the measured wall-time bottleneck, but reconciliation is not cleanly idempotent. Existing changelog history has duplicate entries for several experiment artifacts, so docs appenders should be keyed by milestone and experiment id.
questions_answered.what_tooling_changes_would_speed_next_mi: Use nonzero-success gate predicates, same-verdict retirement, terminal activation-time gate artifacts, DualGPURunner scheduling, per-experiment GPU telemetry, focused test clusters, and idempotent changelog/roadmap appenders.

bottlenecks_identified: Weak gate predicate: full-pipeline work launched on repair_executor_deployed rather than accepted_repair_count > 0 or repaired_case_success_rate > 0.
Duplicate same-verdict pipeline churn consumed 25 minutes / 62.5% of the supplied wall time.
Legacy Exp 1269 arXiv Bundle v10 dependency consumed 10 minutes / 25% of wall time instead of becoming an activation-time terminal state.
SOTA GGUF cache/provenance preflight still consumed a scheduled runtime slot rather than a fast readiness check.
Both RTX 3090s were idle at closeout, so GPU capacity was unused and DualGPURunner was not evidenced as active.
No GPU zombies were present; the resource loss was scheduler idleness, not leaked VRAM.
Full-suite/spec-coverage debt remains too red for blanket gating, even though it was not the largest observed timing item.
Docs reconciliation is append-only but not idempotent enough, creating duplicate changelog noise.
Timing attribution is not self-contained: the .110 operational prompt reused .109 repair/arXiv experiment IDs, which makes retrospective analysis depend on operator-supplied timing context.
improvements_suggested: Gate full-pipeline reruns on accepted_repair_count > 0 or repaired_case_success_rate > 0, not on executor deployment alone.
Add same-verdict retirement for pipeline artifacts within a milestone; suppress exact reruns until a dependency artifact changes.
Convert Exp 1269/arXiv Bundle v10 into an activation-time terminal GATE_BLOCKED artifact unless upstream critical-fix or credentialed-submission state changed.
Make SOTA GGUF cache/provenance preflight a sub-second structured check with explicit model cache/provenance fields.
Persist gpu_monitor.py before/after snapshots into every GPU-bearing result artifact, including utilization_pct, VRAM used, process count, and wall time.
Use DualGPURunner by default for Qwen/Gemma local SOTA lanes when both RTX 3090s are free.
Run independent CPU and docs tasks in parallel with GPU-bearing work after phase-0 gates are satisfied.
Keep preflight tests focused by failure cluster until the full suite and spec coverage are green enough for blanket gating.
Make ops/changelog.md and docs/roadmap.md appenders idempotent by milestone and experiment id.
Persist a conductor activation snapshot into results/ so operational retros do not rely on mutable roadmap files or cross-milestone timing labels.

top_3_highest_leverage_actions.action: Gate full-pipeline validation on nonzero validated repair success
top_3_highest_leverage_actions.rationale: The three Full-Scale Pipeline v3 entries dominated the timing. If the repair executor has zero accepted repairs, large pipeline validation should be blocked and replaced with a repair root-cause task.

top_3_highest_leverage_actions.action: Terminalize the Exp 1269 arXiv legacy gate at activation time
top_3_highest_leverage_actions.rationale: The arXiv path is a known serial gate. If upstream state has not changed, the conductor should emit a terminal blocked artifact immediately.

top_3_highest_leverage_actions.action: Add GPU telemetry and DualGPURunner scheduling enforcement
top_3_highest_leverage_actions.rationale: Both GPUs were idle with no processes. Telemetry would expose silent sequential fallback, and DualGPURunner would allow Qwen/Gemma lanes to run concurrently when live inference is required.

savings_basis: The supplied slowest five account for 37 of 40 minutes, but some replacement diagnostic work remains useful. A conservative estimate is 55% faster next milestone after eliminating weak-gate pipeline churn, terminalizing legacy arXiv/cache checks, and overlapping independent CPU/GPU work.

preflight_suite.assessment: The supplied top-five timing does not identify the unit/lint suite as the primary bottleneck. Test and spec-coverage debt should still be handled as bounded clusters because blanket preflight gates remain risky.

doc_reconciliation.assessment: Doc reconciliation was not the slow path, but duplicate changelog rows in recent history show appenders need milestone/experiment-key idempotency.

meta_reflection: The main efficiency issue is not raw experiment speed. It is evidence quality at the gate boundary. A wired repair executor, a stale arXiv dependency, or a partially known model-cache state should not be enough to spend runtime on large downstream tasks. The next milestone should make the conductor distinguish 'available' from 'useful' before scheduling expensive validation.
